name: NICE NG51: High-Risk Sepsis Criteria (Extreme Tachycardia with Tachypnea in Infection)
description: Suspected infection with Heart Rate > 130 bpm and Respiratory Rate >= 25 breaths/min indicates high-risk sepsis.
section_number: Table 1: High risk criteria for adults aged 18 and over with suspected sepsis

consequent.clinical_action: Immediate 112 / 108 ambulance transfer to hospital emergency department for sepsis six bundle implementation.
consequent.clinical_rationale: Severe physiological disturbance in the context of infection carries high mortality risk requiring immediate emergency resuscitation.

name: NICE NG51: Moderate-to-High Risk Systemic Signs (Fever with Moderate Tachycardia)
description: Fever > 38.3 C with Heart Rate > 100 bpm in an adult.
section_number: Table 1: Moderate to high risk criteria for adults

consequent.clinical_action: Urgent medical review within 2 to 4 hours in an ambulatory or primary care setting.
consequent.clinical_rationale: Systemic response to infection without immediate organ failure signs warrants prompt same-day clinical assessment.

name: WHO Adult Triage: Mild Isolated Fever without Physiological Derangement
description: Isolated mild fever with preserved vitals (normal HR, normal RR, normal SpO2) and no danger signs.
section_number: Module 2: Secondary Survey and Safety Netting

consequent.clinical_action: Self-care with oral hydration, antipyretics, rest, and strict red-flag safety-netting advice (return immediately if breathing worsens or confusion develops).
consequent.clinical_rationale: Mild pyrexia with completely stable cardiorespiratory vitals and absence of distress can be safely observed at home initially.
